clue.text: Skin condition left over after hospital in dispersal of cancer

indicators.note: 'in' puts the hospital group inside the scrambled word that follows
something dispersed is scattered, so the letters of that word are spread into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then scattered

indicators.note: placing one thing after another strings them together in sequence

parts.note: H is the map-sign abbreviation for hospital
L is the standard abbreviation for left
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A doctor describes a skin complaint lingering after a hospital stay during treatment for cancer.
explanation.walkthrough: H with L and O after it goes inside a rearrangement of CANCER, giving C-HLO-RACNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Chloracne is an acne-like eruption caused by exposure to chlorinated chemicals, so it is a skin condition.

clue.text: Crook with card concealing queen

indicators.note: to conceal is to hide inside, so the first word wraps the queen

parts.note: to card wool is to comb it
R stands for Regina, queen

explanation.surface: A criminal holding a playing card with a queen up the sleeve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crook' and 'card' suggest a cardsharp; card is the verb for combing wool.
explanation.definitionFit: Cromb, also crome, is a dialect word for a crook or hooked stick.

clue.text: Grain crop giving many people starters for usual meals

parts.note: a horde is a large crowd

indicators.note: starters come first, so only the opening letter of each following word is kept

parts.note: the opening letters of both words

explanation.surface: A harvest that feeds a crowd its everyday dinners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starters' looks like the first course of a meal; it picks out initial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Hordeum is the botanical genus of barley, a cereal grown as a grain crop.

clue.text: Clue — it's contrived, pestilential (and unjustifiable)

indicators.note: something contrived is artificially put together, so these letters are reassembled

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A solver complains that the clue is forced, pernicious and indefensible.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket is Azed flagging that the sense 'pestilential' is one Chambers marks as a wrong use.
explanation.definitionFit: Luetic properly means syphilitic, from Latin lues, plague; Chambers records the loose sense pestilential as unjustified.

clue.text: Broadcaster delivering farewell, on time, within quota (12, two words)

indicators.note: 'within' puts the farewell and time inside the allowance word

parts.note: a ration is a fixed allowance
adios is Spanish goodbye
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A presenter signs off punctually inside the allotted airtime.
explanation.definitionFit: A radio station is an organisation that transmits programmes, so it is a broadcaster.

clue.text: Company grub served up: bones

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company

indicators.note: 'up' in a down clue means read from the bottom, so the food word runs backwards

parts.note: eats is slang for food

explanation.surface: A firm's canteen dishes up a plate of bones.
explanation.definitionFit: Costae is the Latin plural of costa, a rib, so the word names bones.

clue.text: Attempt to impress in garden pomp laid out

indicators.note: a garden laid out is arranged to a new plan, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Showing off with a grandly landscaped garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link to the garden, but it is part of the letters rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Name-dropping means mentioning famous acquaintances casually so as to seem important.

clue.text: Sequence I'll appear in is drying up

indicators.note: the letter will appear inside the next words, so it is placed within them

parts.note: to sere is to dry up or wither
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener notes the stage at which a plant begins to wither.
explanation.definitionFit: A series is a number of things coming one after another, which is a sequence.

clue.text: Source of fever, most serious drugs, first to be avoided

indicators.note: avoiding the first means leaving out the opening letter of the phrase

parts.note: Class A is the UK legal category for the most harmful drugs

explanation.surface: A doctor blames a fever on the hardest drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassa is the Nigerian town that gave its name to Lassa fever, where the virus was first identified.

clue.text: Section of cabin he restored is natural

indicators.note: a section is a piece cut from a longer stretch, here a run of the following letters

parts.note: the letters running across the three words

explanation.surface: Part of a cabin that a man restored keeps its natural look.
explanation.definitionFit: To inhere is to be inherent, existing as a natural part of something.

clue.text: Right page in book wife follows for thickening in recipe?

indicators.note: the wife comes after the page, so the two parts are joined in that sequence

parts.note: RO is short for recto, the right-hand page of a book
UX is the abbreviation of Latin uxor, wife, used in legal documents

explanation.surface: Cookbook instructions: find the right page, and the wife takes over to make a thickening.
explanation.walkthrough: UX for wife is an obscure abbreviation of Latin uxor found in Chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: A roux, cooked flour and butter, is the classic base used to thicken sauces in a recipe.

clue.text: Tropical African plant Gabon developed at edges of river (7, two words)

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit at both edges of the river, enclosing it
a country that has developed has changed its form, so the letters of the name are rearranged

parts.note: the country's name, to be rearranged
EA is an old dialect word for a river or running water

explanation.surface: A tropical plant from Gabon grows along a riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Developed' reads as describing a nation's economy, but it scrambles the country's name. EA, a river or stream, is an old dialect word kept in Chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Goa bean, or winged bean, is a climbing legume of the tropics that Chambers places in Africa.

clue.text: Clan left out of highland ghylls?

indicators.note: something taken out of a word is removed from it

parts.note: ghylls are ravines; in the Scottish Highlands they are glens
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A Highland clan has left its ravines.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition by example: ghyll is a northern English word, glen its Highland equivalent.
explanation.definitionFit: A gens was a Roman clan, a group of families sharing a name.

clue.text: Nymphs are dancing in e.g. Horatian verses

indicators.note: 'in' places the dancing word inside the verses that follow

parts.note: Horace is famous for his Odes

indicators.note: dancing letters move about, so the word that dances is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Nymphs dance through the lines of Horace's poems.
explanation.definitionFit: Oreades is the Latin-style plural of oread, a mountain nymph of Greek myth.

clue.text: It may suggest Romney is disfiguring horse's head

parts.note: to mar is to disfigure; 'is disfiguring' is the third-person form

indicators.note: a head is the front end, so only the opening letter of the animal's word is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of horse

explanation.surface: The politician Mitt Romney is blamed for spoiling a horse's head.
explanation.walkthrough: Romney sounds like the US politician, but it is Romney Marsh, the flat coastal area of Kent famous for its sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Romney Marsh is a stretch of Kent coastland, so the word marsh calls Romney to mind.

clue.text: Astute about earth, prepare for colder times

indicators.note: 'about' means going around, so the first word wraps the second

parts.note: astute means shrewd or wise
to earth is to bury, which is to inter

explanation.surface: Advice to a shrewd gardener readying the soil for the winter months.
explanation.walkthrough: Earth is a verb here: to earth something is to bury it.
explanation.definitionFit: To winterise a house or car is to make it ready to cope with cold weather.

clue.text: Scots well-to-do, not the last in essence

indicators.note: 'not the last in' tells you to drop the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: a thing's being is its essential nature

explanation.surface: A Scottish moneyed class, not quite at the core of things.
explanation.definitionFit: Bein is a Scots adjective for comfortable or well-off, the same idea as well-to-do.

clue.text: E.g. conference held in deep earnest

indicators.note: something held in the following words is contained within their run of letters

parts.note: the letters spanning the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: A conference conducted with deep seriousness.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital-free 'conference' reads as a meeting; it is the Conference variety of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Conference is a popular British variety of pear, so the fruit is exemplified by it.

clue.text: Suckers she's bamboozled about a bit of tat?

definitions.text: Suckers she's bamboozled about a bit of tat?

indicators.note: 'about' means going around, so the jumble wraps the next piece
bamboozled means confused, so these letters are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then jumbled
taken as written, then jumbled; the 's is 'has'

indicators.note: only a bit, the opening letter, of the next word is wanted

parts.note: the opening letter of tat

explanation.surface: A saleswoman has fooled gullible buyers over some cheap goods.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a woman who has conned suckers into buying tat. Tat is British slang for cheap, tasteless goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A hucksteress is a female huckster, a pedlar who sells cheap goods with sharp patter.

clue.text: A girl he's taken out displaying superior dressing (7, two words)

indicators.note: taken out on a date, the words go out of order and are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl a man has taken on a date shows off a smart outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Superior' means upper: it is a dressing for the top of the head, not a fine one.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair gel is a styling product applied to the hair, a dressing for the topmost part of the body.

clue.text: Jock's undershirt made by company in coarse cotton

indicators.note: 'in' places the company abbreviation inside the cloth word

parts.note: surat is a coarse cotton cloth named after the Indian city
CO is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A Scotsman's vest is made by a firm out of rough cotton.
explanation.walkthrough: Jock is crossword shorthand for Scottish; the Scottish sense is the undergarment, not the medieval tunic.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers gives surcoat in Scots use as an undervest, an undershirt.

clue.text: Sign of Japanese family, lacking heart (does one hear?), living the high life

indicators.note: asking whether one hears it tells you the pieces are to be judged by their sound, not their spelling

parts.note: a mon is the crest or badge of a Japanese family
a tick is a sign, the mark put against a correct item
someone lacking heart is callous; said aloud, the tail of the answer approximates it

explanation.surface: A Japanese clan's emblem, for a family without compassion, enjoying luxury in high society.
explanation.walkthrough: This parse is tentative: read 'Sign of Japanese family' as the family's tick after MON, and say MON-TICK-CALLOUS aloud to approximate the answer. 'The high life' suggests luxury; it means life on the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: Monticolous describes plants or animals that dwell on mountains, so their habitat is literally high up.

clue.text: It stops one informing on crooked mate that's run in

parts.note: o' is a short form of on, as in o' nights

indicators.note: something run in is brought inside, so the race letter goes within the friend
crooked means bent out of shape, so these letters are twisted into another order

parts.note: taken as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A criminal's code keeps him from grassing on a bent partner who has been arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run in' means arrested, which suits the crooked mate; here it only puts R inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Omerta is the Mafia code of silence, which forbids members to inform to the police.

clue.text: Italian holding roller aloft to force entry

indicators.note: holding something means having it inside, so the nationality wraps the next piece

parts.note: IT is the abbreviation for Italian

indicators.note: aloft means raised high, and in a down clue a word lifted up reads from the bottom

parts.note: a purr is a low continuous rolling hum, as a cat makes

explanation.surface: An Italian lifts a garden roller to break down a door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roller' suggests a heavy object; it means a rolling sound.
explanation.definitionFit: To irrupt is to burst in forcibly, as an invading crowd forces its way inside.

clue.text: Work period cut short, accepted most favourable conditions

indicators.note: a word cut short loses its final letter

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
a period is a span of time
A is the abbreviation for accepted, as on bills

explanation.surface: Reduced working hours were accepted as the best terms on offer.
explanation.definitionFit: Optima is the plural of optimum, the conditions best suited to growth or success.

clue.text: Lissomest will regularly display such practices

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the word is taken

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: The most supple people will habitually show off certain exercises.
explanation.definitionFit: Isms are distinctive doctrines or practices, named from the suffix that labels them.

clue.text: Bad shot was degrading (about fifth from rough)

indicators.note: 'about' means going around, so the sinking word wraps the chosen letter

parts.note: to degrade is to sink in quality or standing

indicators.note: the fifth from a word is the letter in fifth position

parts.note: the fifth letter of rough

explanation.surface: A golfer's poor stroke was humiliating, the ball ending up in the rough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rough' and 'shot' set a golf scene; rough only supplies a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf a shank is a mishit off the club's hosel, sending the ball sharply sideways.

clue.text: Wally getting award for fine play?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an old slang word for a simpleton
second meaning: the American theatre prize given for outstanding plays

explanation.surface: A twit somehow wins a prize for acting.
explanation.walkthrough: A wally is British slang for a fool. Chambers keeps the same name, formerly slang for a simpleton, from Antony.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadway's Tony Awards honour the best stage plays, and the old slang word also meant a fool.

clue.text: One disembarks from jet with a spring in one's step

definitions.text: with a spring in one's step

indicators.note: someone who disembarks leaves the vessel, so a letter is removed from the following word

parts.note: a jet of water is a spray
A means one, as in 'a pound'

explanation.surface: A passenger stepping off a jet airliner with a jaunty walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jet' suggests a plane, which makes 'disembarks' natural; it is a jet of liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: Spry means lively and nimble, as of someone walking briskly despite age.

clue.text: St Mirren's formerly given run around by playin' Celtic

indicators.note: something with others running round it is enclosed, so the answer sits inside the next words

parts.note: the letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A Scottish football report: St Mirren, run ragged by Celtic.
explanation.walkthrough: St Mirren is a Paisley football club, so the definition asks for the Scots word; Celtic is the Glasgow club, not a language.
explanation.definitionFit: Yince is the Scots form of once, meaning formerly, as a St Mirren fan might say.

clue.text: It switches current or the flow in e.g. cable

indicators.note: 'in' places the rearranged letters inside the example that follows

parts.note: a cable is a kind of thick rope

indicators.note: letters in flow are fluid and do not stay put, so these two words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: An electrician's device that controls current, or the flow in an electric cable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cable' reads as electrical wiring in this surface; here it means a stout rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A rheotrope is an old name for a commutator, an instrument for reversing the direction of an electric current.

clue.text: Trimmed turns in college entertainment?

indicators.note: something that turns faces the other way, so the words after it are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
a rag is a student charity carnival held by British colleges

explanation.surface: Shortened acts appear in a student revue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turns' looks like a noun for variety acts; it is the verb that flips the following pieces. A rag is a British student fundraising event.
explanation.definitionFit: Garni is a French-derived culinary term meaning garnished, that is trimmed with accompaniments.

clue.text: Making one fortification metre short at front

indicators.note: a word short at the front lacks something at its start, so a letter is dropped there

parts.note: an obsolete sense of munition is a fortification or defence
M is the abbreviation for metre

explanation.surface: Building a defensive wall that falls a metre short at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Unition is an old word for uniting or joining into one, from the Latin for one.

clue.text: Field of medicine not good? This may measure system disorder

parts.note: ENT is ear, nose and throat medicine
ropy is British slang for poor quality or unwell

explanation.surface: A doctor asks whether a specialty is failing, and how to gauge a body's disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'System disorder' sounds medical; it is the physicist's measure of disorder in a closed system.
explanation.definitionFit: In thermodynamics, entropy is the quantity that measures the degree of randomness in a system.

clue.text: Range of modern computers (mica chips)

indicators.note: a stone that chips breaks into fragments, so the mineral's letters are broken up and reset

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Modern computers are built with silicon chips; here the chips are of the mineral mica.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chips' reads as microchips, which suits computers; here it is a verb breaking up the mineral.
explanation.definitionFit: The iMac is Apple's line of all-in-one desktop computers.

clue.text: Fashionable neck/breast of lamb turning on end of rotisserie, whole

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'

indicators.note: a cut turning on a spit faces the other way, so its word is read backwards

parts.note: target is a butcher's term for the neck and breast of lamb

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, the only one kept

parts.note: the final letter of rotisserie

explanation.surface: A smart restaurant roasts a whole cut of lamb on a turning spit.
explanation.walkthrough: TARGET as a cut of lamb is an old butcher's word recorded in Chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: Integrate as an adjective means whole or complete, the sense kept in integer and integral.
